record.paper_title: Orthogonality Types in Normed Linear Spaces
record.original_question: Let X be a Banach space of dimension at least 3, and write S_X for its unit sphere. Is X necessarily a Hilbert space if every closed homogeneous hyperplane H in X admits a unit vector x in S_X such that x is Pythagorean-minus-orthogonal to all unit vectors of H, meaning x ⊥_{P-} y for every y in H ∩ S_X, where x ⊥_{P-} y means ∥x - y∥^2 = ∥x∥^2 + ∥y∥^2?

evidence.quote: Question 4.7.17 Let X be a Banach space, dim X ≥ 3, such that for any closed and homogeneous hyperplane H ⊂ X there exists x ∈ SX such that x ⊥P− Hx ∩ SX . Is X necessarily a Hilbert space?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let (X, ‖·‖) be a real Banach space with dim X ≥ 3, and let S_X = {x ∈ X : ‖x‖ = 1} denote its unit sphere. For x, y ∈ X, define the Pythagorean-minus orthogonality relation by

  x ⊥_{P−} y  ⇔  ‖x − y‖² = ‖x‖² + ‖y‖².

Assume that for every closed homogeneous hyperplane H ⊂ X (i.e., every closed linear subspace of codimension one), there exists a unit vector x ∈ S_X such that

  x ⊥_{P−} y  for every y ∈ H ∩ S_X.

Must X be (isometrically isomorphic to) a Hilbert space?
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a Hilbert-space characterization problem via Pythagorean-minus orthogonality on hyperplanes. Available literature discusses related characterizations (e.g., via I-, IP-, P-vectors, transitivity, almost transitivity) but no source found resolves this specific hyperplane-Pythagorean-minus condition. It appears to be an open problem.

status_evidence.title: Orthogonalities, transitivity of norms and characterizations of Hilbert spaces
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizations of Hilbert spaces via I-, IP-, P-vectors require additional transitivity assumptions.
status_evidence.claim: Related Pythagorean-orthogonality Hilbert-space characterizations require extra hypotheses; the hyperplane condition is not resolved here.

status_evidence.title: Birkhoff-James orthogonality and applications: A survey
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of orthogonality types and open questions in normed linear spaces.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys on orthogonality in normed spaces list open Hilbert-characterization problems.
